name: needle
description: Automation foundation model for tiny devices: 2-bit, 8-29 MB, tool calls, structured extraction and embeddings on phones, wearables, smart homes, robots, cars and microcontrollers.
one_liner: A tiny AI brain — small enough to run on a smartwatch, smart speaker, or even a basic microcontroller — that can understand simple spoken or typed commands and act on them, with no internet connection required.
buyer: A smart-home or wearable device manufacturer who wants voice/text command understanding on-device, without sending user data to the cloud or paying per-request API fees.
business_use_cases: A smart home device maker adds offline voice command parsing ("turn off the lights in the bedroom") without a cloud round-trip.
A wearable fitness tracker startup adds simple typed/voice command support that works with no phone connection.
A robotics or industrial IoT company uses it for structured data extraction from sensor readings or operator commands directly on the device.

money_ideas.idea: License the model per device shipped to hardware manufacturers.
Offer custom fine-tuning services for a manufacturer's specific product commands and vocabulary.
Support/maintenance subscription for companies embedding it in shipped products.

steal_this: Build a demo this weekend: a $20 microcontroller kit that responds to 5 voice commands entirely offline, and pitch it to a smart-home hobbyist hardware maker as a proof of concept.
